visual.titulo: Mercury concentration rises up the food chain

turnos.t: Bioaccumulation is the build-up of a persistent pollutant within a single organism over time. Biomagnification is the increase in concentration at successively higher trophic levels, because predators eat many contaminated prey.

Minamata Bay in Japan. From 1932 to 1968 a chemical factory released methylmercury. It biomagnified through fish and shellfish to the people who ate them, causing severe neurological disease, recognised in 1956. And microplastics, particles smaller than 5 millimetres, carry other pollutants up the food web.
